summary: Fixed all three harness defects: named a consolidated end-of-run failure roster, added a committed known-failures.txt baseline with EXPECTED/NEW classification, and removed the dominant wall-clock cost via --skip-slow on all 5 redeploy-checkpoint call sites (measured 13m48s -> 2m4s per invocation). Also fixed a shared stale-fixture bug clearing 3 of the 8 originally-named failures.

artifacts.summary: All 6 phases completed: stale-fixture fix, failure roster, regression test, known-failures.txt manifest, --skip-slow wall-clock fix, and documentation reconciliation.

user_decision.question: This task added --skip-slow to all 5 orchestrator redeploy-checkpoint deploy_findings_snapshot call sites, removing the dominant measured wall-clock cost (13m48s -> 2m4s per invocation). During implementation, research turned up that a prior task in this repo (documented in batch-orchestration-guardrails.md's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint section) had already investigated and REJECTED a weaker version of this same idea (sharing one Gate-8 capture between pre/post) because ~40 of ~73 core test suites resolve their subject-under-test from the DEPLOYED tree, not source-store -- meaning this checkpoint's full-depth pair was the only thing verifying those suites pass against a freshly-deployed tree. This task's --skip-slow change is a stricter version: those ~40 suites now get zero coverage from this checkpoint against a fresh deploy. Should this trade-off be accepted as implemented, or should Phase 5 be reverted (restoring the wall-clock cost) pending a narrower follow-up fix?
options: Accept as implemented -- keep --skip-slow on all 5 call sites; the measured wall-clock win (a single dispatch previously consumed ~45 minutes and terminated without writing its handoff) is judged to dominate the residual gap, which is now flagged in code comments, shell-script-testing.md, batch-orchestration-guardrails.md, and this summary's Follow-ups for a scoped future fix

Revert Phase 5 (drop --skip-slow from all 5 call sites, restoring the full-depth pre/post pair and its ~13m48s cost per invocation) until a narrower fix -- running only the ~40 deploy-tree-first suites against gate 8 post-redeploy -- is built as a separate follow-up task
user_decision.recommended: Accept as implemented -- keep --skip-slow on all 5 call sites; the measured wall-clock win (a single dispatch previously consumed ~45 minutes and terminated without writing its handoff) is judged to dominate the residual gap, which is now flagged in code comments, shell-script-testing.md, batch-orchestration-guardrails.md, and this summary's Follow-ups for a scoped future fix
